messages:
evan: Quick follow-up to the modularization RFC. I'm proposing a 'tessellation' pattern: carve the monolith into small, well-scoped tiles with explicit adaptor boundaries and a short-lived compatibility plane. Trying to capture operational guardrails and a debt amortization schedule.
meera: Tessellation = interesting name. How does this differ from previous slice/corridor approaches?
evan: Main differences: 1) each tile has an explicit amortization budget (tech-debt $ or weeks) that must be spent before GA; 2) an automated compatibility plane that can run in read-only mode to detect divergence; 3) tighter drift telemetry per-tile.
alon: Amortization budget sounds useful. Who sets it? product or platform?
eera: (meera) I'd vote product for the budget size, platform enforces the countdown and the compatibility checks.
sasha: Need concrete examples of the compatibility plane. evan?
evan: Simple adapter that records field-mapping diffs and schema drift. Runs in parallel during cutover, emits 'delta' reports every 30m and blocks GA if schema drift > 5 fields or missing required fields. config snippet: 
```
compatibility:
  mode: observe-only
  report_interval: 30m
  drift_threshold: 5
  block_on_missing_required: true
```
meera: Nice. On KV/caching: proposal is to lean tiles toward owning their local read-cache when they're on the hot path. Shared enrichment tiles can use eventual snapshots. We'll require a priming job before traffic cutover.
sasha: Testing and rollout plan?
evan: Multi-stage: 1) bench + contract tests in CI, 2) shadow traffic in staging with compatibility plane on, 3) tenant canary with 1% traffic and watchdog for 48h, 4) ramp per-tenant with amortization timers enforced. Abort conditions: p95 latency up by >15%, error spike >0.5%, or drift reports fail to converge.
alon: How do we prevent config sprawl and too many one-off flags?
evan: Central tile registry + a single flagstore for tile toggles. UI will show timer and amortization remaining. Platform owns flagstore and exposes a small CLI.
ops-bot: scheduled: ci/tessellation-compatibility -> staging-run at 2026-06-10T02:00:00Z
meera: Ownership: product teams own tile business logic and contract tests; platform owns adapters, flagstore, compatibility plane, and rollback tooling.
sasha: Rollback playbook should be <5 minutes to flip flags and drain tile instances. I can draft the script. Sample command: 
```
tilectl revert --tile payment-hotpath --tenant gamma --grace 300
```
alon: On tech-debt amortization: propose a policy that any tile cutover must include a removal plan for the equivalent legacy code or a tagged TODO with an expiry and owner. If expiry passes, infra can automatically disable the legacy path.
evan: I like the automatic expiry enforcement. Helps avoid drift. Also propose a small monthly "amortization review" where teams report progress.
meera: Observability: dashboards per-tile: latency histograms, schema-drift rate, cache-hit rate, token spend delta, and rollback events. Also export a weekly tile health summary.
sasha: Perf harness: we should have a lightweight replay tool that can run a production sample against the new tile in staging for 24h. Include a KV priming stage.
evan: Security note: tiles must declare data-sensitivity level. Private tiles (PII) require extra audit logs and separate KV tenancy.
ops-bot: job queued: infra/tile-priming -> staging at 2026-06-11T09:45:00Z
alon: Timeline suggestion: 1 week design + signoff, 2 weeks prototype, 1 week contract-test adoption by owning teams, then staggered tiles every 2 weeks. Amortization windows vary (2-8 weeks) depending on complexity.
meera: One risk: small tiles increase operational overhead. Mitigation: group related tiles into a managed bundle with a single owner for smaller-features.
sasha: Also guard against noisy metrics causing premature aborts. Add a quiet window during initial canary where alerts are suppressed to reduce flapping, but still collect data.
evan: I'll update the RFC with the tessellation checklist, amortization policy, compatibility plane config, and sample rollback scripts. Posting link when done. Thanks all. :pray:
